infotheory.est.ksg1.headline: JIDT KSG1 MI/CMI driven directly, W in {0,1,2,5,20,85}: max_abs <= 5.3e-15. All 64 SPI ksg runs <= 7.1e-15, including tied data (seeded jitter reproduced by a Python java.util.Random port). DYN_CORR_EXCL excludes |s-t| <= W (counts 31-2W, nearest admissible at W+1, raise at N=4+2W). NUM_THREADS=64=availableProcessors; BIAS_CORRECTION reads None.

infotheory.theiler_window.headline: data.theiler reproduced exactly by a lag loop (12/12, max_abs 0.0, 0 integer mismatches). raw - Bartlett = 1.0000 on 11 pairs (var2 2.6398 vs 1.6398). Grows to ~T/3 on narrowband (22.1/85.4/339.2/1352.9 at T=64..4096). Extra finite-sample upward bias on correlated pairs (gauss_ar1 raw 5.14 vs tau+1 3.63).

infotheory.mi.kraskov.headline: From-scratch <= 4.4e-15 (7/7). Kernel mi_ksg1 with no jitter 3.6e-15. sklearn KSG1 0.0-1.3e-15 (external-pkg). Converges to -0.5ln(1-rho^2): pair (2,3) 0.5379/0.4990/0.5084 vs 0.5108 at T=256/1024/4096, |z| <= 1.31. Null z -1.60.

infotheory.mi.kraskov_DCE.headline: From-scratch <= 7.1e-15 (10/10, W up to 339). The window raises MI from 1.442 to 2.254 on narrowband T=1024 and from 0.230 to 0.606 on logistic T=256. On gauss_ar1_pair the DCE expectation is 0.1697 vs 0.1572 without DCE (population 0.1578).

infotheory.tlmi.kraskov.headline: From-scratch <= 5.3e-15. A[i,j] = I(x_i(t); x_j(t+1)): delayed_noise 2.323 vs -0.004. Truth z <= 0.50. The supplement's 'undirected' label conflicts with the asymmetric output (max|A-A.T| 2.33).

infotheory.tlmi.kraskov_DCE.headline: From-scratch <= 6.2e-15 (7/7). Direction 3/3. Truth z <= 0.65. Window rule as for theiler_window.

infotheory.te.kraskov_k-1_kt-1_l-1_lt-1.headline: From-scratch <= 3.1e-15. gauss_ar1_pair converges to 0.0271/0.0524 (pyspi 0.0253/0.0511 at T=4096, z 0.21). Direction 4/4: row = source, logistic_maps_chaotic x->y 0.565 vs -0.074.

infotheory.te.kraskov_DCE_k-1_kt-1_l-1_l.headline: From-scratch <= 2.9e-15 (8/8, W up to 339). Truth z <= 1.83. Direction 4/4.

infotheory.te.kraskov_DCE_k-2_kt-1_l-1_l.headline: From-scratch <= 1.1e-15 (7/7). var2 truth fails at T=1024 (z 2.02, one draw that is fp-exact vs the reference) but passes at T=256 and T=4096. Every copy path computes k=1: 0.1344 instead of 0.1592.

infotheory.te.kraskov_auto-MAX_CORR_AIS_.headline: From-scratch MAX_CORR_AIS reproduces the chosen (k,kt,l,lt) on 5/5 runs and the TE to <= 1.1e-15. Fixed-embedding pyspi with the chosen values equals auto exactly (0.0, 4/4). Documented tau-max-2, implemented 4. Copies compute k=1 TE (0.1336 vs 0.0606).

infotheory.te.kraskov_DCE_auto-MAX_CORR_.headline: Exact incl. the NaN masks: at T=64 narrowband 6/6, logistic 2/2, shared_envelope 6/12 NaN, where T-37 <= 4+2W. The window changes the embedding search (narrowband (2,1,4,1) -> (10,4,10,4)). Fixed == auto 4/4.

infotheory.phi.star_norm-0.headline: Matches the brentq optimum on the analytic derivative to within optimiser tolerance. Population (D15) gap 4.3e-13; D5 gap 2.2e-11. Sample covariances: 37/37 indep runs pass, pyspi - ref in [-3.6e-14, 4.65e-8], max relative 6.4e-4 (beta left at 1 by L-BFGS-B, nit=0 on 67/136 pairs). Monte Carlo of the Eq. 20 definition within 0.52 SE. Octave/PhiToolbox 16/16 (max_abs 4.5e-8). Convergence, null (about 1/T) and 0 <= Phi* <= I all pass.

infotheory.phi.star_norm-1.headline: 21/21 indep runs pass (gap <= 2.4e-8). The identity norm-1 = norm-0 / min past-window Gaussian entropy is exact (max_abs 6.9e-18). The divisor is 1.37-1.43 under z-scoring. On raw scaled_offset it is negative (-0.196), giving Phi*_norm1 = -0.000834 from an Unsigned SPI. definition_under_review true.

infotheory.phi.Geo_norm-0.headline: Population matches the global minimum (D15 gap 3.1e-11, D5 2.5e-10), but the AL fails optimality in 13/37 geo-details runs. It over-estimates at non-stationary stops: up to 1.107 nats on shared_envelope (0,1) T64 (6.532 vs 5.425) and 3.25e-3 on delayed_noise T64. It under-estimates at infeasible stops: cointegrated T4096 -3.46e-4 (relative about 1), and raw scaled_offset -2.34e-5 (relative 0.28, so not scale-invariant). Octave reproduces all of these to <= 3.4e-10, so they are inherited from PhiToolbox. Bounds, null and convergence pass.

infotheory.phi.Geo_norm-1.headline: 17/21 indep runs pass; the failures are the norm-0 AL stalls divided by about 1.42 (delayed_noise T64 2.28e-3). The ratio identity is exact. On raw scaled_offset the value is -0.00106 (divisor -0.196) and also 1.19e-4 from the independent value. Octave 10/10 (1.9e-10). definition_under_review true.

spectral.dtf.headline: Canonical squared DTF fp-exact on the exact spectrum (1.1e-15). The independent chain reproduces all identifiers (rep 21/21, <=7.2e-14). Values are computed per pair on a bivariate model (chain: 0.0887 bivariate vs 0.0682 full-model). The 5-taper estimator has a bias that does not shrink with T: the true direction sits at 0.263 against 0.207, the null at 0.13 against 0, and |z| vs truth grows 4.4 -> 22.2. The direction inverts on delayed_noise. Row = target.

spectral.dcoh.headline: The library returns |H_ij| sqrt(DTF_ij), to 8.9e-16, not Baccala 1998 Eq. 21-22 (checked against the paper). It differs by up to 0.64 per bin, is unbounded (band max up to 2833), is not scale invariant (16.9) and inverts the canonical-DC asymmetry on delayed_noise. Unchanged in v2.0.1; fixed in unreleased upstream master 138f3f7f0f.

spectral.pdcoh.headline: Canonical squared PDC fp-exact (1.1e-15). The 2x2 adjugate identity makes pdcoh == dtf (4.4e-16). The bivariate fit loses the partialisation: on the chain the conditioned PDC(0->2) is 0 against 0.0887 bivariate and 0.2117 in pyspi.

spectral.gpdcoh.headline: Canonical squared gPDC fp-exact (1.0e-15). In 2x2 it equals the canonical squared DC (3.9e-16). Not partial for P>2 (chain: 0 vs 0.0845). It is the only unit that keeps the population direction on delayed_noise, and it is scale invariant within 3.1e-3. Same T-independent bias floor (~0.11).

spectral.ddtf.headline: Computes |ffDTF| x |PDC| (to 4.2e-17) instead of Korzeniewska's ffDTF^2 x pcoh^2 (difference 0.042 per bin). In 2x2 this is |ffDTF| sqrt(DTF), so nothing is conditioned out (chain 0.0091 where the conditioned value is 0). It scales as T^-1/2: slopes -0.506/-0.501/-0.500, spread 1.0%.

spectral.wilson_factorisation.headline: H and Sigma match the independent Wilson on the same CSM (4.3e-13 / 3.3e-16) and the analytic factors (H 3.8e-15; Sigma 3.5e-9, limited by the 1e-8 tolerance). Without zero padding the residual is 0.3-3% (9.1e-5 with padding). Non-convergence and residuals of 0.32-0.61 pass silently. Order and scale non-equivariance up to 3.4e-2 per bin. The NumPy-2 AttributeError depends on rounding.

spectral.sgc.nonparametric.headline: 44/44 impl runs vs from-scratch DPSS+Wilson+Geweke max_abs 3.9e-11 (incl. logistic_maps non-converged, trending 50%-rule NaN cell); library kernel on exact VAR spectrum vs analytic 1.9e-15 / 4.2e-10; T-independent bias: var2 A[1,0] 0.412/0.436/0.402 vs 0.289, null cell 0.10-0.13, conv bias 0.128/0.126/0.125 (T=256/1024/4096), iid null 0.113/0.122/0.126 (NW=10: 0.023, NW=40: 0.0051); mcexp pass; anchor 7 (5 tapers)

spectral.sgc.parametric_order-None.headline: 38/38 impl max_abs 7.7e-14; LWR = direct YW 6.7e-16; order replica exact on 11/11 datasets; truth 7/7 pass (var2 0.313/0.315/0.281 vs 0.289), conv bias 0.0074->0.00065; LWR-OLS 0.0066 (SD 0.030); delayed_noise orders (1,0,0,0,0,0) vs standard Schwarz (1,3,5,2,4,2) -> 5/6 links exactly 0; NaN-BIC non-termination -> ValueError -> TypeError -> all-NaN table; anchor 6

spectral.sgc.parametric_order-1.headline: 38/38 impl max_abs 7.7e-14; LWR = YW 4.4e-16; gauss_ar1_pair truth pass; var2 converges to VAR(1) projection 0.2607 (+ spurious 0.0159 reverse) not 0.2893 (proj 4/4 pass, truth fail z 3.61 @4096); LWR-OLS 0.0030; T=64 delayed_noise: indefinite ecov -> negative cell, true link NaN; anchor 7 (LWR not OLS)

spectral.sgc.parametric_order-20.headline: 41/41 impl max_abs 3.4e-11 incl. T=64; consistent: bias 0.087/0.020/0.0047 (conv ratio 18.5); truth/null fails = small-sample bias of zero-target cells (mcexp pass); T=64 NaN bins 19.8/55.2/65.1%, negatives, var2/gauss all-NaN, every anomaly in an indefinite-ecov pair; LWR-OLS 0.008; anchor 7

distance.dcorr.biased-False.headline: Equals bias-corrected squared dCor R*_n. dcor u_distance_correlation_sqr 8/8 exact, max_abs <= 7.2e-14; from scratch 9/9 <= 7.4e-14. Returns dCor^2, not dCor (0.067-0.250 from sqrt form). Thm 7(ii) convergence 6/6 within 2 SD (max_z 1.63). 60-90% of null pairs negative. Kernel exactly symmetric. One shared-draw T=256 null fail (z -2.03).

distance.dcorr.biased-True.headline: Equals Szekely 2007 dCor_n, unsquared. dcor distance_correlation 8/8 exact, max_abs <= 9.4e-14; distance_correlation_sqr is 0.10-0.25 away. Convergence to sqrt Thm 7(ii) 6/6 (max_z 1.51). Null > 0 with ~T^-1/2 slope (-0.46). Fails: shared T=256 null draw (z -2.60) and circle detection at T=256 (z 4.37 < pre-set 5, though above all 200 permutations).

distance.hsic.biased-False.headline: Stored value is HSIC_u(K,L)/sqrt(HSIC_u(K,K)HSIC_u(L,L)) with x-only median bandwidth. Matches Song eq.5 (<= 2.7e-14), Gretton eq.3 (<= 6.8e-14) and R route on dHSIC Grams (dhsic raw HSIC_b = python to 1.5e-16). Stored/raw 8.4-18.8x. y kernel uses x's gamma (6.2e-16). Process-order dependence up to 0.026 (5.8%) after z-scoring. Population normalised HSIC 4/4 within 2 SD.

distance.hsic.biased-True.headline: Stored value is sqrt(normalised HSIC_b). Rebuilt from dHSIC 2.2 dhsic, it matches 5/5 to <= 2.4e-14 (stored 0.1891 vs raw HSIC_b 0.00276). Same x-only bandwidth: reversed process order changes values by up to 0.0195. Population sqrt normalised HSIC 4/4 within 2 SD. Null > 0. One shared-draw T=256 null fail (z -2.85).

distance.hhg.headline: pyspi equals the from-scratch Heller, Heller & Gorfine 2013 statistic bit for bit (max_abs 0.0) on all 14 continuous-data runs (T64, T256, T1024 pair). Analytic N(N-2)(N-3) holds exactly (242048, 16451072). The null mean matches the analytic n(n-2)(n-3)/(n-1). max|A-A.T| = 0.0 everywhere, so a Directed class carries no direction. On tied data, sklearn dot-product distances change T by up to 4.88e-2 relative (logistic_maps T256 raw). Not 10 because the supplement/GitBook describe an RKHS/kernel statistic and say undirected.

distance.mgc.headline: The from-scratch MGC with SciPy's constants reproduces pyspi to <= 5.8e-14 (19 def runs). All bivariate_gaussian and iid pairs use the global scale (opt_scale probe), where pyspi equals the column-centred dCorr^{n,n} to <= 3.8e-14 but differs from the unbiased U-centred dCor^2 by 1.8e-3 / 1.6e-4 / 1.2e-5 at T64/256/1024 (near-equal, not equal). SciPy's region rule differs from both the paper and r-mgc and moves values by up to 0.061 on continuous data at T256. 80-90% of iid values are negative despite the 'unsigned' label. Score 6 = deviates from both supplement and canonical (also the same-lineage cap).

distance.dcorrx.maxlag-1.headline: Replica of the code's own computation (_kernels_distance.hyppo_dcorrx_replica): 13/13 runs pass, max_abs <= 6.5e-14. Canonical Mehta/Shen series-slice statistic: 8 runs designed to fail. Lag 0 identical; totals differ by 0.0019 (iid) to 0.0794 (gauss_ar1_pair T1024, 15.6%). var2 lag-1 term 0.1705 vs 0.2378. Direction 8/8: A[i,j] = j -> i. Weighted SUM, max 1.426 (bound 1.996). Null 2/3 pass; the T=256 exceedance (-0.0143 vs band -0.0140, Bonferroni-adjusted empirical p 0.04) is read as chance.

distance.dcorrx.maxlag-10.headline: Replica 13/13 pass, max_abs <= 9.7e-14. Mehta 0/8 by design: totals differ by up to 0.2604 (gauss_ar1_pair T1024, 24.4%) and 0.092 on var2. delayed_noise true-delay terms (d=1,3,5): 0.9746/0.9732/0.9725 vs Mehta 0.9824/0.9809/0.9799 (ratio 0.992). Direction 8/8. Null 3/3. Sum max 6.337 (bound 10.785). T >= 13 needed.

distance.mgcx.maxlag-1.headline: From-scratch MGC matches SciPy's compiled map to <= 3.8e-14 (5 mgcmap runs, tied data included) and pyspi to <= 3.3e-14 (9 replica runs). Same-lineage scipy runs agree exactly (0.0). Lag-0 term equals the pyspi mgc unit to <= 2.7e-15. Mehta 0/5 by design: totals differ by up to 0.0615 (var2). Direction 5/5. Null 2/2. Uses 4 multiscale_graphcorr calls per pair where 2 are needed (50% of the time).

distance.mgcx.maxlag-10.headline: Replica 10/10 pass, max_abs <= 7.0e-14; scipy runs <= 1.1e-16; lag-0 term equals mgc unit to <= 8.3e-16. Mehta 0/5 by design: totals differ by up to 0.0984 (gauss_ar1_pair, 20%). Direction 6/6, including lags 3 and 5. Null 2/2. Sum max 7.973 (bound 10.785). 13 calls per pair where 11 are needed.

distance.dtw.constraint-None.headline: 16/16 dp runs bit-identical to own DP (max_abs 0.0); dtaidistance 4/4 max_abs 0.0. Against Sakoe-Chiba 1978 (abs cost, diagonal weight 2, divide by n+m), iid T1024 pair (0,1) pyspi 22.50 vs 0.417, ratio 24-55, Spearman 0.77-0.96. Null T1024 22.04 vs MC 21.84+-0.25

distance.dtw.constraint-itakura.headline: 16/16 dp bit-identical; tslearn parallelogram equals exact-integer mask at T 64-4096 (0 cells differ); global-only parallelogram is 18% (median) below local-slope DTW on iid noise

distance.dtw.constraint-sakoe_chiba.headline: 16/16 dp bit-identical; dtaidistance window=2 exact; band |i-j|<=1 at every T (3T-2 cells); delayed_noise dtw/Euclid 0.084 / 0.724 / 0.731 for delays 1 / 3 / 5

distance.lcss.constraint-None.headline: 17/17 dp bit-identical to Vlachos S1 (eps=1, <=); strict < gives identical values; null means 0.788/0.803/0.810 match MC (max_z<=1.86)

distance.lcss.constraint-itakura.headline: constraint ignored: bit-identical to lcss in 6/6 runs; 13/16 dp runs fail vs masked LCSS (iid T1024 pair (0,1) 0.8037 vs 0.0); tslearn torch backend equals the masked reference exactly

distance.lcss.constraint-sakoe_chiba.headline: constraint ignored: bit-identical to lcss; 10/16 dp fail vs band-1 masked LCSS (iid 0.8037 vs 0.7061, delayed up to 0.28); masked null 0.715+-0.009 vs pyspi 0.80-0.82 (max_z 8.2)

distance.softdtw.headline: softdtw matches Cuturi-Blondel Alg.1 to max_rel 2.5e-14 (16/16); constraint identifiers bit-identical to softdtw in 32/32 runs (KNOWN bug 3); 8/8 fail vs masked soft-DTW; every z-scored value at T1024 is negative (-454 to -174), Spearman with the divergence 0.44-0.60

distance.gwtau.headline: The from-scratch merged-quantile W2 over 46 def runs (21 datasets, kernel/pipeline/pipeline-detrend paths, T 64-4096) agrees with pyspi to max_rel 1.2e-13. POT 0.9.7.post1 ot.wasserstein_1d agrees to 1.9e-15. Closed forms for sampled sinusoids (f 0.1 vs 0.4, f0=0.25 phase grid, EEG frequencies) agree to <= 4.6e-11. pyspi equals the paper's Def. 2 times sqrt(T/(T-1)) exactly: canonical/pyspi = sqrt((T-1)/T) to 2.2e-16, so pyspi is 0.79% higher at T=64 and 0.012% higher at T=4096. This is the authors' MATLAB root-exclusion convention. Symmetric bitwise (max|A-A.T| = 0.0, including the unmirrored probe). Null value grows as sqrt(T) (slope 0.570; Monte Carlo 0.502; analytic E[gwtau^2] |z| <= 1.66).

causal.ccm.E-1.headline: pyEDM.CCM(random=False) kernel equals own simplex_crossmap in 12/12 runs, max_abs 1.65e-14. Seed-42 wrapper: 8 of 11 statistical runs within 2 se; excursions |z| 2.99, 2.16, 2.04. The 16-seed bias test passes (|z| <= 1.55), so the excursions are sampling noise and there is no bias. Reported quantity is the supplement's mean/max summary, not a convergence test. Static dependence: 0.967 vs -0.003. Direction: 3 pass, 2 fail (bidir, var2).

causal.ccm.E-10.headline: Kernel exact in 15/15 runs (E=3,4,10), max_abs 1.94e-14; exclusionRadius=10 exact (<=4.4e-16); affine 1.2e-15. Wrapper: 11/12 statistical runs within 2 se; T=1024 one cell at |z| 2.06. Curves pass (chi2 p 0.78/0.45). Direction is lost at T=256 (chaotic -0.0034, sugihara -0.1086) and recovered at T=1024 (+0.6432); var2 points the wrong way (-0.2434), as the kernel also does.

causal.ccm.E-None.headline: EmbedDimension rho(E) table reproduced from scratch (<=1.0e-15). pyspi passes E=10 while the argmax-rho E is [1,2]/[10,7]/[9,3] (known bug 2). Output is bitwise equal to E-10, and its 9 stat runs pass. At the documented E=2 the reference gives 0.199/0.687 vs pyspi 0.284/0.281 (stat-mean-docE fails as expected, max_z 408.6).

infotheory.est.kozachenko.headline: <=2000 rows: JIDT = canonical Euclidean KL to 7.1e-15 (noise off) and = java.util.Random(42) jitter replica to 6.2e-15. >2000 rows: naive NN routine gives wrong distances (d=10 3981/4087 points), entropy low by -0.038 (d=5) and -4.334 nat (d=10) at N=4096; port reproduces to 2e-14. NORMALISE inert; 'linear' label. The <=2000-row computation alone would rate 9.

infotheory.je.kozachenko.headline: kl 5/5 (max 1.3e-7), jrand 6/6 exact (1.2e-14), T4096 unaffected (2e-8); population 6/6 (max_z <=1.82); exactly symmetric; near-tied shared_envelope rows set by the jitter (shift 2 ln 100)

infotheory.ce.kozachenko.headline: A[i,j]=H(x_j|x_i): kl 5/5 (1.4e-4), jrand exact 1.7e-14; population 6/6 (max_z <=1.27); asymmetric (0.262 on anm) despite the 'undirected' doc keyword

infotheory.xme.kozachenko_k1.headline: H(y_t|x_{t-1}) exact (jrand 2.1e-14); no documented definition, no cross mapping; k=2 uses the same lag set (diff <=2e-3); population 5/6 (one draw at z 2.01)

infotheory.xme.kozachenko_k10.headline: 9 source lags (lag-10 copy 1.50506 = 9-lag design, 10-lag 0.689); d=10 KL bias +1.5 nat on delayed_noise; T'=2011 jumps -1.646 (0.1976 vs 1.4489); T4096 -0.048 vs 1.329

infotheory.cce.kozachenko.headline: Kramer CCE with n=5 (documented 10) exact for T<=1024 (3.7e-14); population pass at T256/1024; T4096 low by 1.97-2.61 nat (defect; truth z 13.2)

infotheory.di.kozachenko.headline: pyspi = Massey DI_5 + B(target) to 3.7e-14 (B_KL 0.165/0.315 on var2; 2.52/2.77 on independent random walks); n=5; T4096 iid pair 2.613 vs 0.028 (defect)

infotheory.si.kozachenko.headline: Ay SI exact (jrand 4.1e-14); population 3/3 on gauss_ar1_pair (MC SD 0.118 at T1024); sign-varying null; T4096 defect effect 2.2e-3; one draw at z 2.52

infotheory.est.kernel.headline: Direct JIDT entropy (d=1..10) / MI / TE (k=1,2) at widths 0.5 and 0.25 = numpy box kernel to <=2.6e-13 (N-1 SD; a ddof0 variant is off by 0.029/0.007 bits, nats by 2.39/3.56). Tie grid: 15 values match the closed box with self-inclusion to 8.9e-16 (H=2.2879430946, open box 3.3219). Bin search = compare-to-all (0.0). 1-D statistical runs: 3 of 5 tail fails (max_z 2.93/2.26/2.30).

infotheory.je.kernel.headline: 12/12 exact runs <=4.1e-14 in bits, incl. kernel path and detrend. Kernel path on raw scaled_offset = z-scored + log2(sd_i sd_j) to 7.1e-15. All values in [0, log2 T]. Fresh fill exactly symmetric. iid mean 3.741/3.989/4.066 vs box limit 4.0987, truth 4.0942.

infotheory.ce.kernel.headline: 10/10 exact runs <=3.0e-14. A[i,j]-A[j,i] = H(x_j)-H(x_i) to 0.0. Never negative. rho=0.8 pair: 1.055/1.262/1.344 vs box limit 1.3486, truth 1.3101.

infotheory.mi.kernel.headline: 10/10 exact runs <=1.6e-15. Fresh fill exactly symmetric. rho=0.8 pair: 1.297/0.898/0.775 vs truth 0.737. Null: 0.693/0.242/0.099 bits. Nonlinear pairs 1.646/1.205 vs cross pairs <=0.032.

infotheory.tlmi.kernel.headline: 8/8 exact runs <=2.2e-15. Direction delayed_noise 2.647 vs 0.064, var2 0.305 vs 0.101. On the delayed_noise pair the 0.25 box caps the estimate at about 2.65 (truth 3.33). One tail fail (z 2.16).

infotheory.te.kernel_k-1_kt-1_l-1_lt-1.headline: 10/10 exact runs <=1.3e-15; the next-value box reuses the past width (own-SD variant <=0.0049 bits). Direction passes on delayed_noise, var2 (T256/T1024), chaotic and sugihara. The l/k_tau/l_tau variants all equal k=l=1 (3.3e-16). Null 1.51/1.06/0.50 bits. One tail fail (z 2.48).

infotheory.xme.kernel_k1.headline: 8/8 exact runs <=2.7e-14 for H(x_j(t)|x_i(t-1)). history_length=2 equals k=1 shifted by one sample (6.2e-15). Direction delayed_noise 0.180 vs 2.024. gauss_ar1 1.863/1.740 vs Gaussian 1.864/1.796.

infotheory.xme.kernel_k10.headline: 7/7 exact runs with lags 1..9 (<=1.2e-12); the 10-lag variant differs by up to 0.073. At least 99% of points are alone in the 10-D box, so |values| <=0.024 bits on stochastic data (truth 2.047). The var2 ordering is reversed (one direction FAIL). Informative on chaotic logistic maps (0.977 vs 1.777).

infotheory.cce.kernel.headline: 7/7 exact runs <=7.9e-13. Configured n=5 vs documented 10; n=10 changes the value by only -0.005. Terms 3-5 collapse: iid per term 2.01, 1.70, 0.68, 0.10, 0.01 vs 2.047 each; sums 2.39/3.44/4.50 vs 10.24. Direction passes on all 3 datasets.

infotheory.di.kernel.headline: 8/8 exact runs <=8.0e-13. pyspi = box Massey DI_5 + B(target) to 0.0 (B 0.882/0.846). Independent white pairs give 5.55/5.83/5.31 bits (truth 0). n=10 gives 11.5. Ordering preserved on delayed_noise, var2 and chaotic.

infotheory.si.kernel.headline: 7/7 exact runs <=7.4e-14. Fresh fill exactly symmetric. gauss_ar1 0.728/0.322 vs population 0.144. Null 1.74/0.93/0.40 bits.

misc.gpfit.DotProduct.headline: Posterior arithmetic matches the analytic ridge / Bayesian linear regression at sklearn's theta to max_rel 7.4e-15 (z-scored data) and 2.0e-13 (raw cointegrated); f_bar elementwise <= 1.25e-12. On z-scored data pyspi equals the global ML-II optimum to 2.4e-9; polish gain <= 8e-13; multistart gain <= 1.5e-12. Value = ((T-1)/T)(1-r^2) to <= 6.1e-5 (T64), 3.8e-6 (T256), 6.9e-8 (T1024); symmetric to <= 8.1e-15. On raw data sklearn's single start stops up to 7.5e-5 below the ML-II maximum (MSE <= 1.35e-4 relative); an own single start reproduces pyspi to 2.4e-9. Score 7 is the cap for an optimiser unit passing optimality.

misc.gpfit.RBF.headline: Posterior arithmetic matches an independent GP at sklearn's theta (max_rel 4.0e-11); an own single L-BFGS-B start from theta=0 reproduces pyspi on 14/14 runs (max_rel 2.1e-7). Own multi-start ML-II finds a higher LML on 99/128 pairs and changes the value on 98; the better optimum interpolates on 72 (MSE = (w'/(1+w'))^2 mean(y^2) to 5.5e-11). Local polish fails marginally on 2/12 runs (gain 1.85e-3, 1.31e-3; MSE <= 6.7e-6). RBF in-sample MSE exceeds the linear Ridge MSE on 30/50 pairs (by <= 0.0063). Direction: A[i,j] = MSE of x_j predicted from x_i (nonlinear_dependence 0.026 vs 0.996).

misc.coint.johansen_order-0_ardiff-1.headline: Unrestricted-constant Johansen (case 3) LR statistics for r=0. Matches the kernel exactly (19/19, max_rel 1.35e-12), textbook case-3 RRR (8/8, 5.2e-14) and urca ca.jo ecdet='none' K=2 (8/8, 3.3e-13). Truth: cointegrated (0,1) trace 111.0/386.1/1628 vs 95% value 15.49 at T=256/1024/4096. statsmodels table = case 3 (cvmc max z 1.07). Driftless null: trace over-rejects (0.10/0.135). Not 10 because 'ardiff'/'maximum eigenvalue' wording is a naming convention.

misc.coint.johansen_order-0_ardiff-10.headline: Same as k=1: kernel 19/19 (2.5e-13), case-3 RRR 8/8 (2.0e-12), urca ecdet='none' K=11 8/8 (3.5e-12). Truth fails at T=64 (m=53; (0,1) 12.81/12.92 below 14.26/15.49, a power limit) and passes at T>=256. Driftless null trace rejection 0.1225/0.150.

misc.coint.johansen_order-1_ardiff-1.headline: statsmodels/LeSage full-sample OLS pre-detrending, reproduced exactly by urca ecdet='none' on detrended levels (8/8, 9.6e-14). No native ecdet/spec matches. Max_rel vs restricted-trend case 4 (ecdet='trend') is 0.025/0.124 at T=256 and 0.26/0.34 at T=4096 (max-eig/trace, null pairs). Vs unrestricted-trend case 5: trace 2.0e-3 -> 4.8e-4. det_order-1 table = case 5 (cvmc max z 1.31). Driftless null trace rejection 0.19/0.21.

misc.coint.johansen_order-1_ardiff-10.headline: Same scheme: urcadt 8/8 (7.6e-14). Vs case 4 max_rel trace 0.195/0.053/0.38 at T=256/1024/4096; T=256 pair (1,0): pyspi 27.186/32.915 vs case 4 27.512/35.644. Vs case 5 trace 0.024/5.7e-3/7.1e-3. Driftless null trace rejection 0.21/0.22.

misc.coint.aeg.headline: Canonical Engle-Granger ADF t-ratio is exact vs the kernel (36/36, 1.6e-13) and vs R lm + urca ur.df at the selected lag (12/12, 6.5e-14). But the 'undirected' SPI fixes the regressand by channel index: reversing channels changes all 6 cointegrated entries by up to 1.53 (T=256); the reverse orientation differs by 7.41 on iid T=256 and 60.87 on trending T=4096. bivariate vs multivariate: -61.24 vs -0.36. Raw negative t on an Unsigned class; -inf for collinear pairs.

misc.ids.headline: Estimator equals the paper's IDS_inf (Eq. 6/11/12, k=6, B=1). 14 kernel kids runs agree to <= 7.8e-16 and 10 pipeline/detrend runs to <= 2.2e-15. The own Eq.6 transcription matches the kernel mirror to <= 1.0e-15. Bandwidths 0.25/0.5/1.0 and pnorm 1/2 match Eq.6/12 to <= 4.4e-16. Identical pair = 1 exactly. Population 0.2641/0.7349 (quadrature); 6/6 truth runs within 2 MC sd (max_z 0.93). Null MC mean*sqrt(T) about 2.07; pyspi off-diagonal mean 0.2354/0.1135/0.0647/0.0324 at T=64/256/1024/4096; 4/4 pass. Score 7 because pyspi z-scores while the paper's reported setting min-max scales to [0,8]: values differ by up to 0.680 (nonlinear_dependence 0.943/0.993 vs 0.485/0.313 at T=4096). Symmetry max|A-A^T| = 2.2e-16.

wavelet.psi.headline: Independent replica reproduces all six identifiers to 1.0e-12 (106/106 rep runs); the library PSI(t) matches the replica to 2.3e-13. The stored value depends only on cached PSI(t) at t in freq_id (0..9 full, 0..1 low, 2..9 high; change elsewhere 0.0, tsel). Reversing input x[:, 37:] changes every stored value by exactly 0.0 (winperm-tail 3/3), while x[:, :10] changes them by 0.56-5.81 and x[:, 10:37] by 0.12-4.13 (input horizon 36/28 = max t_sel + 27). The documented all-time quantity misses on 36/36 runs (max_abs 0.07-6.06) and the intended smoothed-coherency Nolte PSI on 12/12 (0.51-5.55). Sign agreement with the true lead/lag: mean-full 0.40 and max-full 0.10, against 1.0 for the intended quantity. The null SD of mean-full is constant in T (1.29/1.27/1.28) while the SD of the all-time mean falls as 0.32/0.13/0.06. The stored matrix is exactly symmetric (0.0 over 247 runs).

wavelet.morlet_cwt.headline: 125 wavelets of length 1, W = sqrt(2) +- 2 ulp. The direct-convolution CWT is bitwise x*W0 and the FFT CWT is within 2.7e-15 of sqrt(2)x. Fixed grid with 21 low-band bins. Cache ignores fs: fs=10 on a shared Data returns the fs=1 result (-1.5e-18 vs fresh 0.0224). Orientation conn[hi,lo] = X_hi conj X_lo confirmed on an independent CWT.

wavelet.cohmag.headline: 1.0 everywhere (16/16; max identifiers 1+2^-52); from-scratch matches. Canonical n_cycles 7, pair (1,0): 0.658 narrowband, 0.969 delayed, 0.298 bivariate, 0.076 iid. narrowband_f0-0.1: 0.149 on pyspi grid vs 0.9998 on documented grid.

wavelet.phase.headline: Identity pi(n+ - n-)/N exact to 3.6e-15. A 4.4e-16 input change moves the value by up to 0.175 (0.1367 -> -0.0383). numpy.fft replay differs by up to 0.32. Under channel reversal A_rev = -A + 2 pi n(Im=0,Re<0)/N within 6.1e-16.

wavelet.icoh.headline: Round-off: max identifiers up to 2.41e-12 at T=1024 (4 runs fail the trace's 1e-12 bound; T=64 <= 1.7e-13). From-scratch exactly 0. A_rev = -A exactly. Canonical ImC 0.47 / -0.67.

wavelet.plv.headline: Exactly 1.0 (16/16, max_abs 0). Canonical single-trial PLV 0.66 narrowband, 0.93 delayed, 0.24 bivariate, 0.057 iid.

wavelet.ppc.headline: -inf everywhere (16/16). The from-scratch pipeline with Im exactly 0 is also -inf (c*fl(1/c) residues). The library _PPCEst gives +inf from ratio 1.1e-8, while the audit data max ratio is 2.41e-12.

wavelet.pli.headline: pyspi = 1 - frac(Im csd == 0), exact on 16/16 runs: 0.85-0.875 at T=64 and 0.988-0.992 at T=1024 regardless of coupling. From-scratch gives 0. Re-z-scoring moves the value by up to 0.0099 and the numpy.fft replay by up to 0.027.

wavelet.dswpli.headline: -inf everywhere: -inf at Im==0 points, NaN elsewhere (666/31334 at iid T256). Synthetic input gives NaN without an exact zero. Class name says Weighted but computes the unweighted pli2_unbiased.

wavelet.wspli.headline: Bitwise equal to pli for all six identifiers, every dataset and T. 'squared' in the name, but the computation is the unsquared wPLI.

wavelet.dwspli.headline: Exactly 0.0 (16/16) from the zero-denominator guard, also from-scratch. Canonical epoched dwPLI^2 0.65 narrowband, 0.95 delayed.
